task: PERF-2 (inline /synthesize event-loop block), COR-B-2 (task cancelled while waiting for a resource slot was resurrected/rendered anyway), COR-B-4 (_cancelled_tasks set leak)

app/api/tts_api.py.summary: PERF-2: the inline (<500 char) branch of POST /synthesize now runs orchestrator.submit(task) via starlette's run_in_threadpool instead of calling it directly on the async handler. orchestrator.submit() is fully blocking (admission loop with time.sleep, HTTP dispatch, retries); calling it inline froze the whole asyncio event loop for the request's duration, stalling every other API request, /jobs poll, and websocket broadcast. Response shape/behavior unchanged; only the background_tasks.add_task long-text branch was already off-loop and is untouched.

app/orchestration/scheduler/orchestrator.summary: COR-B-2: submit() now registers the task in a new `_waiting` registry (task_id -> (task, stop_event)) BEFORE entering the resource-admission wait loop, guarded by a new `_registry_lock` (the first lock ever added around `_active`/`_waiting`; `_active` mutations now go through the same lock). cancel() checks `_waiting` as well as `_active`; finding a task there sets its stop_event (and pops the entry) instead of returning False. The admission loop checks stop_event (and, defense-in-depth, whether the job's DB status has independently flipped to 'cancelled' via `_is_task_cancelled_in_db`) at the top of every iteration and again right after an admission succeeds (closing the race where a slot frees at the exact instant of cancellation) — in either case it returns without dispatching, releasing resources first if they were actually just reserved. Poll wait changed from `time.sleep(1.0)` to `stop_event.wait(1.0)` so a concurrent cancel() is observed immediately instead of after the full 1s interval. Previously, cancel() only ever checked `_active` (populated AFTER admission succeeded), so a task still spinning in the admission wait was invisible to cancel() — the caller's fallback (`update_job(status="cancelled")`) never actually stopped it, and once a slot freed, submit() dispatched a full render of the 'cancelled' job anyway, then published status="completed" force=True over it.

app/tts_server/server.py.summary: COR-B-4: `_cancelled_tasks` changed from a bare `set[str]` to a `dict[str, float]` (task_id -> cancellation monotonic timestamp). `cancel_task` now sweeps entries older than `_CANCELLED_TASK_TTL_SECONDS` (300s) on every call via the new `_sweep_cancelled_tasks` helper. Previously the set was only ever cleaned up in the /synthesize finally block for a matching task_id, so a task cancelled but never synthesized (a fan-out child cancelled before its own /synthesize runs, or a job cancelled while still queued) left a permanent entry -- unbounded growth over server uptime. `_is_task_cancelled` semantics unchanged for any cancellation within the TTL window; the normal cancel->synthesize->discard flow is unaffected (discard -> pop).

flow_impact: No change to the synthesis/queue contract shapes. PERF-2 only affects where orchestrator.submit() executes (threadpool vs event loop) for the external TTS API's inline path. COR-B-2 closes a cancel-vs-admission-wait race in the Studio 2.0 job lifecycle (orchestrator owns job execution lifecycle, unchanged ownership split). COR-B-4 is an internal TTS Server memory-bound fix with no externally observable behavior change within the TTL window.
